children: Abu Dhabi Tourism Investment Company (ADTIC) has completed the first phase of renovations at Mercure Hurghada in Egypt as part of a hotel refurbishment programme valued at more than $100 million across Hurghada and Sharm El Sheikh.
The completed works include the hotel's entrance, reception area and lobby, ahead of its planned rebranding as Mövenpick Hurghada in early 2027, the company said in a statement.
The $100 million-plus renovation programme covers completed and ongoing works at the company's hotels in the two Red Sea destinations.
Approximately 80 percent of the refurbishment works at Mövenpick Sharm El Sheikh have also been completed, the statement said.
The company said its hotels were recording occupancy levels exceeding 90 percent, with strong demand expected during the Christmas and New Year period.
ADTIC is also progressing with the construction of the Sofitel Legend Pyramids, located opposite the Grand Egyptian Museum and overlooking the Pyramids of Giza.
The company is preparing additional hotel developments, including a 450-room property in Hurghada and a 500-room hotel in Sharm El Sheikh.
It is also planning a 120-room extension to the existing Mövenpick Sharm El Sheikh.
The three projects would add a combined 1,070 rooms to the company's portfolio, including the planned extension.
ADTIC is 84 percent owned by the Abu Dhabi Development Fund, with additional shares held by the Abu Dhabi National Hotels (ADNH) and Egypt's Ministry of Public Business Sector.
In November 2023, Zawya Projects had reported that ADTIC is investing $161 million in hotel projects in Egypt including the renovation of existing properties.
(Writing by Marwa Abo Almajd; Editing by Anoop Menon)
